correctionsThisCycle.what: TWO UNTRACKED ARTEFACTS WERE SITTING INSIDE SERVED URL SPACE. Found this cycle, moved out this cycle, and the class is now refused by a suite. This is a real defect, not a tidy-up.
correctionsThisCycle.detail: A zero-byte emitter scratch file and a 5.6 KB dotfile DRAFT of the status feed, one in each of the two served feed directories. The publish directory is the repository root, so both sat at real public paths. They survived every existing gate for one reason: they were UNTRACKED. The deploy-safety and root-serving gates both reason about TRACKED files and about the repository ROOT; neither looks inside a served subdirectory for untracked residue. A directory publish would have served an internal draft of the status feed publicly. Both were renamed out of URL space into force-404'd space, and a new suite now enforces an ALLOWLIST — anything in a feed directory that is not the feed itself fails, including file types nobody has invented yet.

correctionsThisCycle.what: This is the SECOND time a temp file has been found in the publish tree, which is why a gate was written instead of a cleanup.
correctionsThisCycle.detail: The previous cycle untracked two emitter temp files that had been committed. This cycle found two more that had never been committed, and so were invisible to any tracked-file check. The recurring class is 'the emitter leaves scratch beside its output'. Remembering has now failed twice; an allowlist cannot forget.

correctionsThisCycle.what: TWO UNMERGED BRANCHES WERE TRIAGED AND DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED, because merging them would have REVERTED newer work. Recorded because 'unmerged' is not the same as 'owed'.
correctionsThisCycle.detail: Two 2026-08-04 flywheel branches are not ancestors of the shared branch, which reads at a glance as two owed merges. Checked first-hand instead: every file they introduce is already present on the shared line, and the shared line's copies are NEWER — its status emitter was last written 2026-08-05 02:54, against branch tips of 08-04 20:50 and 08-04 21:41. Their content arrived by another path. Merging either would overwrite the current emitter with an older one. They are superseded ancestors and are left unmerged on purpose.

mainRef.reason: Reproduced again this cycle against the real remote, not carried forward: the code host refused with 'could not read Username'. There is no credential helper, no token in the environment and no code-host CLI. Every reference here is a last-known LOCAL read and is labelled as such. Presenting a local reference as a live read is the exact dishonesty Rule 14 forbids.
mainRef.aheadCountCaveat: 33 is the count measured at the moment the cycle-121 merge landed. Committing this feed adds one more, so a reader checking afterwards will correctly see 34. Stated this way on purpose: a hard number that its own commit invalidates is a number that is wrong every time it is read.
